record.original_question: If G is a bounded semitopological group, or more generally a bounded quasitopological group, must G have countable cellularity? Here a semitopological group is a group whose topology is invariant under both left and right shifts, a quasitopological group is a semitopological group with continuous inversion, and bounded means both left bounded and right bounded.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(G,\tau)$ be a group endowed with a topology $\tau$. Call $(G,\tau)$ a semitopological group if multiplication is separately continuous, i.e., $\tau$ is invariant under all left and all right shifts $x\mapsto ax$ and $x\mapsto xa$ for $a\in G$. Call $(G,\tau)$ a quasitopological group if it is a semitopological group whose inversion $x\mapsto x^{-1}$ is continuous.

A subset $S\subseteq G$ is called left bounded if for every neighborhood $U$ of the identity $e$ there is a finite set $F\subseteq G$ with $S\subseteq FU$, and right bounded if there is a finite $F\subseteq G$ with $S\subseteq UF$. The group $G$ itself is called bounded if it is both left bounded and right bounded as a subset of itself.

The cellularity of a topological space $X$ is the supremum of cardinalities of families of pairwise disjoint nonempty open subsets of $X$; $X$ has countable cellularity if every such family is at most countable.

Question: Must every bounded semitopological group $G$ have countable cellularity? More generally, must every bounded quasitopological group have countable cellularity?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not yield a definitive resolution of Protasov's question on whether bounded semitopological (or quasitopological) groups must have countable cellularity. Related work by Protasov and others addresses cellularity and resolvability in bounded groups and balleans, but no specific source confirming a solution to this exact problem was located.

status_evidence.title: Selective survey on Subset Combinatorics of Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Protasov surveys combinatorial size of subsets of groups, with cardinal invariants such as cellularity arising by analogy with topology.
status_evidence.claim: Protasov has studied cellularity-type invariants of bounded groups but the specific question on bounded semitopological groups is not reported as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Cellularity and density of balleans
status_evidence.snippet: Studies cellularity as a cardinal invariant of balleans, an asymptotic counterpart of uniform topological spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related cellularity questions in the asymptotic/bounded setting are actively investigated, without an explicit resolution of the semitopological-group version.
